description: The National StormSmart Coasts Network: Linking Coastal Decision Makers to Resources is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Climate Adaptation Knowledge Exchange (CAKE); EPA, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency; NOAA Office for Coastal Management. The StormSmart Coasts Network launched in 2008 in Massachusetts and expanded to include Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Louisiana, Mississippi, New Jersey, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, and Texas. The program (now known as StormSmart Connect) provides local coastal communities and decision-makers with up-to-date and relevant information on storms, flooding, sea level rise, and climate change. Coverage: Coffeyville, KS (2008). The toolkit gives Coffeyville, KS as the location, 2008 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
